text.p: These are the headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Poll predicts slim majority for Chretien: 38 percent of decided voters favor Liberals, survey finds, confirming party's steady decline in popularity.
- Unease riddles BQ, PQ heartland: Core voters show grudging support.
- NATO deal hailed as symbolic healing: Officials hope partnership treaty with Russia will match success of Marshall plan.
- Rejected by voters, French PM quits: Election made it clear Juppe had to go.
- Rock orders investigation of cover-up allegations: Dealings between judge, bureaucrat in Nazi cases to be probed.
- Eaton's renovations hit snag: Retailer's plan to spend millions on store makeovers irks creditors who fear high costs.
- Tax break looks doomed for charitable looan-backs: An Ottawa proposal would outlaw the donation of cash, but retention of its use by having a foundation lend it back to your business.
- Placer to sell 2 Quebec mines to 'unknown': Tiny McWatters must find C$70 million.
- U.S. pushes for stringent bribery rules: Wants OECD nations to prosecute.
- Eaton's sales keep sliding: Confidential report to key lender shows year-to-date turnover at the troubled retailer has fallen, despite a sharp increase in spending on advertising.
- Molson looks set to unload Beaver, Home Depot.
